Grit, screenings, and a portion of the material skimmed from the treatment processes is disposed of in the Redwood Sanitary Landfill.
Biosolids are ultimately disposed of onsite at the Discharger’s 9-acre land disposal site.

The onsite reclamation system consists of two 20-acre storage ponds, a 20-acre freshwater marsh/wildlife pond, and 200 acres of irrigated pasture. The storage ponds are used to dechlorinate the effluent through natural processes.

Since 2012, the Discharger has operated its own onsite water recycling facility. The Las Gallinas Recycled Water Facility produces disinfected tertiary recycled water by further treating the secondary effluent using ultrafiltration and ultraviolet disinfection.

The existing rock biofilters and nitrification fixed film reactor will be replaced with a combined fixed film/activated sludge nitrification/denitrification system, with associated sludge collection systems. This new treatment process will increase the peak wet weather biological treatment capacity from 8 MGD to 18 MGD.
The existing deep bed filters will no longer be used for treatment prior to discharge, but the filter effluent channel will continue to serve as the influent wet well for the Recycled Water Facility.
A primary effluent pump station will be constructed to lift primary effluent into the new secondary treatment facilities.
Two mechanical disc thickener units will be constructed to thicken the combined primary and secondary sludge stream.
The existing chlorination and dechlorination storage and feed facilities will be upgraded, and modifications will be made to the chlorine contact chamber piping.
